t: Maximize Grid Happiness: Profile DP Over a Sliding Row Frontier
o: We fill an m x n grid (both at most 5) with at most introvertsCount introverts and extrovertsCount extroverts — possibly fewer — maximizing summed happiness. Introverts pay 30 per orthogonal neighbor; extroverts earn 20, so an introvert-introvert edge loses 60 in total, a mixed pair loses 10, and two extroverts gain 40. Interactions are strictly local: only the previous n cells can still acquire new neighbors as we sweep row by row, so a base-3 code of one row (0 empty, 1 introvert, 2 extrovert) is a complete frontier summary. Remaining people counts (each <= 6) complete the state, giving roughly 25 x 243 x 7 x 7 tiny DP states. Example 1 reaches 240 by isolating the introvert (120) and stacking the two extroverts adjacently (40+20 twice); example 2 shows four introverts in a 2x2 block each suffering exactly one neighbor for 4*120 - 8*30 = 240.
k: Happiness decomposes into per-edge terms plus bases: I-I = -60, I-E = -10, E-E = +40 — charge every edge once when its later endpoint cell is placed.
A base-3 mask over the trailing n cells plus remaining counts of each person type fully determines all future interactions.
Placement scoring looks only at the left and up frontier digits, so each transition is O(1).

a.i: Walk cells in reading order making three choices per cell: leave empty, seat an introvert, or seat an extrovert. When seating, resolve interactions immediately with the already-fixed left and up neighbors, adding base happiness plus pairwise adjustments. Memoize on (cell index, previous row mask, current partial row, introverts left, extroverts left); the partial row is just cur * 3 + type, so keys stay small and reachable states collapse far below the theoretical maximum.
s: Recurse over flattened index idx with prevRow mask, partial cur mask, and remaining budgets.
Digit lookups: up neighbor = digit c of prevRow; left = cur % 3 when c > 0.
Seating type t adds BASE[t] (120 or 40) plus, for each occupied neighbor nb, GAIN[t] + GAIN[nb] with GAIN = (0, -30, 20).
When c == n-1 the completed row becomes prevRow (cur * 3 + t) and cur resets to 0.
Return max over the three choices; memoize every call.
a.t: O(m * n * 3^n * 7 * 7) states with O(1) work each — under 100k transitions at the constraint limits.
a.sp: O(m * n * 3^n * 7 * 7) for the memo plus recursion depth O(m * n).

a.i: The same state space iterated forward instead of recursed: dp[mask][in][ex] holds the best happiness after processing some cells with a given frontier mask and people used. Each cell shifts every stored mask left by one trit and appends nothing/intro/extro. Rolling arrays keep memory to two layers, and there is no recursion overhead — useful when the scoring rule changes, since transitions are pure data manipulation.
s: Initialize dp[0][introvertsCount][extrovertsCount] = 0 with NEG everywhere else; size masks by 3^n and use p3 = 3^(n-1) for the shift.
For each cell index i, reset ndp to NEG.
Extract up = mask / p3, left = mask % 3 when column c > 0, and shifted base sbase = (mask % p3) * 3.
Push the empty choice to ndp[sbase], introvert (120 minus penalties vs up/left) to ndp[sbase+1] with budget decrements, extrovert (+40 with gains) to ndp[sbase+2].
After all cells answer max over dp of every entry.
a.t: O(m * n * 3^n * 7 * 7) — each cell relaxes every (mask, budget) entry with three constant-time choices.
a.sp: O(3^n * 7 * 7) — rolling double buffer of one layer each.

w: In an interview, present the edge-decomposition insight first (-60/-10/+40), then either implementation; Approach 1 is usually faster to write correctly because the memo absorbs reachability automatically. Pitfalls: forgetting that cells may stay EMPTY (you are not forced to place anyone); charging an adjacency only once instead of to both participants; masking errors when a row completes versus mid-row shifts. Edge cases: zero counts on either side must still yield 120/40 bases correctly, and grids smaller than the people count simply leave extras unseated. Follow-ups: maximize happiness subject to using ALL people, or support a third personality type — both are one extra dimension in the same profile DP.
